# evidence-review

Review semantic applicability, calibrate observations and investigate scoped tool evidence.

Use [guide.md](guide.md). Only controller-loaded references are available; links do not grant file access. Return the requested typed proposal; request missing source.

SEMANTIC REVERSE REVIEW
Review actual materials, not just the generator's rationale. Separately examine (1) applicability of the goal to the current API/configuration/fault contract; (2) necessity, sufficiency, alternatives and conditions of the obligation and support relation; (3) correspondence of the formal checker to the intended responsibility when a model is supplied.
For each target cite the actual source IDs, explain the relevant expectation or dependency, seek contrary or weaker/stronger contracts, and state alternative mechanisms. Ask whether the goal's bad outcome could still occur while the current obligations all hold. A successful model check does not answer that question.
For checker correspondence inspect the actual predicate, trigger, context/identity comparisons, allowed initial states, excluded branches and observed events. Can the antecedent occur? Does the scope contain the relevant event? Do not claim nonvacuity or behavioral equivalence without an executed check; state missing evidence and request discriminating material or exploration.
No issue found is a provisional scoped interpretation, not a proof or an independent consensus vote. A new invocation of the same backend can share the same mistakes. Do not strengthen or weaken a property solely to match the current code or a passing test.

SCOPED DISPOSITION AND REVISION
Only revise existing objects explicitly listed in this review task. The controller computes the actual semantic write set, including binding associations and unit scope. Declare every changed field with exact JSON before and after values in changes. Fields that do not change must not be listed. Changing grounding or applicability does not require changing the claim text. Extra objects need a separate review; newly added candidates are not approved by this review.
For needs_reading, disputed or revision_needed, propose a finite reading/revision/investigation follow-up if supported. If none is legally actionable, explain the missing capability or material instead of inventing a request. Invocation completion does not resolve an issue. Address named open issues using resolves_issue_ids and an attributed resolution_rationale; address their actual prior evidence. Use supersedes_task_ids only when this review fully covers the old versions, scope, materials and required aspects. A partial review cannot clear other issues. Harness-only changes do not resolve semantic disputes.

When resolution_issue_ids authorize reconsidering a prior model issue, compare prior_issue_models with the current model and its actual recheck. Resolve the stable issue against the corrected current model, without declaring the old model correct. A harness-only change or unrelated model cannot resolve a checker encoding dispute. A changed goal meaning requires F2; unchanged meaning with a different encoding needs an attributed encoding_revision and correspondence review.

Return ReviewReply using the actual review_contract in this packet. It states each target type, version, required aspects, their questions and source dependencies. Do not infer type from IDs or rely on an unstated type-to-aspect mapping. Optional aspects do not replace required ones. Keep negative judgments and unresolved evidence visible. No issue found is provisional, not a proof.
For resolvable semantic errors return an F2 revision with the actual old/new judgment and sources. Relations and applicability conditions can be revised without changing a goal sentence. For field-level changes include changes with target_id, field, old_value_json and new_value_json matching the stored objects and patch exactly. Do not invent a counterexample to authorize F2.
Use requests when actual additional ranges are needed; use exploration_requests for unrepresented responsibilities or handoffs and investigations that could distinguish competing interpretations. Unresolved readings must remain explicit. An F2 revision does not automatically validate the new judgment; it will be reviewed in its new version. Do not modify model behavior or supply a replacement Bundle in this task.

Review only the requested aspects in review_contract. Reused judgments and open issues retain their identities; a different trigger name is not new evidence. Put unresolved conditions that affect this judgment in limitations or keep the related ReviewIssue open. scope_limitations are independent boundaries of the audit, not renamed counterarguments. When resolving one issue while other boundaries remain, provide an IssueResolution with its exact stored question/version, actual supporting sources, a specific explanation, independent residual_issue_ids and the retained scope_limitations. A root issue or unresolved child cannot resolve itself by moving to residuals. No-issue judgments are provisional, not correctness proofs. If pending_scope_updates is provided, inspect the actual diff before proposing F2; never silently accept part of a mixed change.

Investigate applicable consensus support and historical constraints:
Which target event matters in this implementation? What identities, context, objects,
and acceptance rules support it? How is that support produced, checked, stored,
transmitted, and consumed? What constraints survive subsequent recovery or context
changes? Use only applicable concepts. Record unestablished boundary guarantees as
relations to their producers or filters, not as automatically valid inputs.
Goals explain audit value, obligations determine check focus, and code determines
model behavior. The graph guides tasks and scope; it is not a proof tree.
